steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Combine garlic powder, seasoning salt, basil, and oregano in a small bowl.

Cook bacon in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until lightly browned and still flexible, 6 to 7 minutes. Transfer bacon to a paper towel-lined plate. Drain any excess bacon grease from the skillet.

Wrap four slices bacon around each tenderloin, securing each strip with 1 to 2 toothpicks. Slice tenderloins between each bacon strip to create a total of eight medallions. Dip medallions into seasoning mix on both sides.
Melt butter and oil together in the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add medallions and cook for 4 minutes on each side.

Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake until pork is no longer pink in the center, 17 to 20 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Bacon-Wrapped Pork Medallions
raw_recipe.description: These pork tenderloin medallions wrapped in bacon make a truly elegant presentation on your dinner plates. Just don't tell anyone how easy they are!

review.reviewBody: This is soooo good! So simple to prepare, yet it looks and tastes like it took a lot of time and effort. I did reduce the seasoned salt to 1/2 teapoon because of a lot of reviews that said it was salty and I think it was perfect. Also, I didn't bother to pre cook the bacon out of laziness, lol, but it cooked up fine in the oven. Other than that I kept everything the same. I will definately be using this recipe again.....and again-YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)

This is delicious! It makes a good presentation, as it looks like filet mignon, yet much cheaper. I cooked until brown in the skillet, then finished in the oven. Cooking the pork in the bacon drippings keeps it tender and very tasty. My husband commented that it was the best pork he has ever eaten!!

This pork was so tender it was like eating a filet. I followed the recipe exactly and it was delicious. I only browned mine for 2 minutes on medium high and then put in the oven for 17 minutes. The were perfect. Not exactly a healthy choice, but a tasty one!

My husband said these were good enough to serve in a resturant. They were really good. I did omit the seasoned salt since the bacon has so much in it to begin with. I dont think the seasoned salt was necessary. Very Good Recipe. Thanks

"Try it, you'll like it," they said. So I tried it. Thought I was in Heaven! Excellent recipe as written with the exception that I like my pork a little pink. Just a little. Many other reviews mentioned the saltiness, so I used only a half tsp of seasoned salt. No other changes. I did use thick sliced bacon for 4 min on my old Geo. Foreman grill, wrapped the tenderloin, cut it into medallions, sauteed them for 3 min per side, put in oven till 142° and let rest. Done! Mashed potatoes and creamed spinach sides. Perfect! Great recipe!

Comments: the beauty of this recipe is that it is so very versatile. You can use varieties of different spices and herbs, fresh or dried, for different tastes and flavors. The use of maple smoked bacon adds a little sweetness that I really liked. Next time I'll use hickory smoked to see the difference. I'll also try a fresh rosemary and thyme blend and maybe Adobe or Montreal seasoning. I also want to slice 2 medallions per slice of bacon, vacuum seal in packs of 2, and freeze to be used for breakfast steaks. Lots of possibilities!!!

Necessities: accurate instant read thermometer, quality bacon, well seasoned cast iron skillet (it does make a difference - mine is 90 years old and has been used continuously).

This turned out well, but I reduced seasoning to 1 tsp each of oregano, basil, and garlic powder only. Bacon is salty enough for dish. I would also reduce cooking time next time as it was cooked a bit much for us. I would sear for 2min each side, then 12 min in oven at 400. as you are only cooking a medallion, the times listed seemed to dry out and over cook the pork.

I liked it and will make it again. Most of the mistake in the dryness was my overcooking in the skillet. As a not so seasoned cook, I need to realize the difference between timing and temperature on each individual's stove. The seasonings should be dusted off a bit so they are not too thick. 
 Also, do not chintz on the oil and butter. My first go around found that I had the thick layer of seasonings burned hard on the pork. Unsightly and dry. 
I also tried a dollop of favorite BBQ sauce on each medallion when I put them into the oven. Finally, I'm forever forgetting how quickly pork tenderloin cooks. With future batches, I'll err to the lesser time in the oven.
Overall, it was quick easy and tasty!
I added onion powder. Herb de Provence. Because I was making 40 medallions, after skillet I placed jam-packed in two 9x13 glass baking dishes. Moist. Tender. Extremely delish!

This recipe is a keeper. The reason for my 4 star rating is the proportions and rations. 1/2 Lb of pork per person is a bit excessive. If you need to reduce the recipe for 2, then, you will have to make couple of adjustments. For 1 lb. tenderloin you will likely need more than 4 bacon strips to wrap it. I had to use the 8 that the recipe called for. Second, you will have to add a bit more of each of the seasonings provided that you will have 8 slices. As for everything else, just follow the instructions or don't do the pre-cooking of the bacon and pre-searing of the medallions. If you go the route without pre-cooking, you will save yourself from the extra oil and will end up with a moister medallion good for the time the tenderloin spends in the oven. As an overall, my actual modification was adding pepper to this recipe. It was delicious! I made a bit of fettuccine and prepared them with the Easy Alfredo Sauce from this site. Perfect combination of restaurant quality dinner at home! Will make it again!

Really enjoyed this. We used a smaller portion of meat, and thick, center cut bacon, which wasn't long enough to wrap all the way around. Two pieces together worked. For the "seasoned salt" we used Cavender's All Purpose Greek seasoning which worked great. 
We found that 2 minutes per side for browning was enough, and wish we had cooked it about 15 minutes instead of 17. It wasn't dry, but more done (at about 160) than necessary.
Definitely a keeper!

The butcher shop in my grocery store sells these as Illini filets (already bacon wrapped). We love these with pickled beets and green beans. A baked potato goes well with also. I rub Worcestershire sauce on each side before seasoning. These turn out great on a foreman grill if anyone still has one

I ... used these directions to cook premade bacon-wrapped medallions. Added some additional lamb grease I had. Before I transferred it to the oven, I filled the remaining space in my pan with steak fries. Omg it all came out so delicious. Great combination of spices and fats for this.

Very yummy. I forgot cook the bacon before I wrapped the pork and it didn’t seem done all way. My husband and I ended up taking most of it off so we could just eat the pork and it was delicious. I needed more seasoning so just improvised by adding to the last few pieces in the skillet and it still turned out great.
No changes. Cooked according to recipe. It was perfect!

This was an excellent recipe I made it at home for a casual dinner with just a family nothing special. It came out very tender juicy but surprisingly salty I'm sure it's just the bacon over bacon after all pork is bacon LOL. 17 minutes and it was already hitting the 153 155 Mark when I took it out of the oven so I figured yesterday if you wanted it 1:43 to 1:50 is take it out after about 15 minutes maybe try 14 but the thing is do it to your taste excellent can't be messed up.
Soooo delicious and tender. Great pork recipe!!

This is a delicious recipe! I tried to submit a photo of my masterpiece, but it was too big. It was a huge hit with my family. The pork is so tender and juicy. The bacon wrapped around it adds another level of flavor. The seasonings are perfect. We can’t wait to have it again!
Absolutely delicious. It presents beautifully for entertaining.
Cut to 3 minutes per side, then oven for 12 minutes in cast iron skillet
